title: Differential retention sampler and just-in-time reveal for trace events
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Our current observability pipeline persists full trace payloads and log snippets indefinitely for a fixed retention tier. This creates unnecessary exposure of sensitive tokens/PII and increases storage/cost. High-fidelity traces are only needed for recent incidents or for a small subset of requests, while long-term analytics can rely on aggregated or pseudonymized data.

Goal: Implement a differential retention and just-in-time (JIT) reveal system for trace events and linked log snippets so that: (1) high-fidelity trace bodies are retained only for a sliding short window and sampled requests; (2) sensitive fields are encrypted/pseudonymized at ingestion and can be revealed only after an RBAC-checked JIT approval with an immutable access log; (3) downstream dashboards and metrics pipelines receive privacy-safe artifacts for long-term storage and queries; (4) tracing hooks annotate redaction decisions to allow reproducible debug flows.

Scope: tracing hooks (span enrichment + export-time masking), ingest-time sampler that tags events for high-fidelity retention or aggregated retention, an encrypted field store with key-wrapping and JIT retrieval flow, RBAC + audit logging for reveals, updates to metrics/log pipelines to accept pseudonymized inputs, and dashboard filter updates for latency/error correlation without exposing raw PII.

Out of scope: complete wide-scale rework of billing telemetry, archival migration tooling, and cross-region key rotation automation (will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Ingest pipeline supports a configurable differential retention policy: sliding window (default 72h) + deterministic sampler for longer retention
Sensitive fields in traces/logs are pseudonymized or encrypted at ingest and stored separately with a JIT reveal API
Reveal API enforces RBAC, records an immutable access entry in audit logs, and requires an explicit justification field
Tracing hooks annotate each span with a redaction decision header and a pseudonym ID for downstream joinability
Long-term metrics and dashboards do not require raw sensitive payloads to reproduce latency/error views
Unit and e2e tests for sampler, redaction, and reveal flows included and passing in CI
Documentation and runbook published, and security review completed and signed off
tasks: Design: finalize retention tiers and sampler algorithm (deterministic hash + rate override)
Infra: extend ingest nodes to run redaction/pseudonymization plugin at SpanExporter level
Storage: add encrypted field store table and key-wrapping metadata schema
API: implement /audit-reveal POST endpoint with RBAC hooks and justification capture
Telemetry: add trace/span annotation schema and update exporter to emit redaction headers
Pipelines: update metrics/logging ingestion jobs to accept pseudonym IDs and drop raw fields for long-term stores
Dashboard: update latency/error dashboards to use pseudonymized joins and add restricted reveal links for on-call
Tests: unit, integration and smoke tests for retention expiry, reveal flow, and audit log generation
Docs: write runbook and developer guide, include example curl flows and RBAC policy snippets
Security: schedule threat model and SRE tabletop for JIT reveal misuse scenarios

notes: Trade-offs considered: encrypt-at-rest with JIT reveals reduces attack surface but adds latency and complexity; to mitigate we adopt an async reveal worker and caching of short-lived plaintext in an ephemeral cache with TTL tied to RBAC session. Deterministic sampling preserves reproducibility for replay and debugging but must be tenant-scoped to avoid cross-tenant leakage. For legal/DSR requests, support immediate erase propagation by linking sampler tags to erasure queues. Next steps: finalize threat model, complete PR with RBAC integration, and coordinate SRE on capacity planning for async decryptor workers.
